title: What customers actually saw
lede: These are screenshots of pages saved by the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine, stored as images. Click one to open the original capture. Captures were found with the CDX API in October 2026. Archived pages from 1999–2000 are often incomplete.[^36]

snips.text: **Nutro MAX Mini Chunk** Regular $26.49 · **Sale $19.99** **Cat gift basket** $29.99 → **$18.99**
“We have closed our virtual doors effective November 9, 2000.… Orders placed before 11am PT on November 9 will be shipped.”
“Welcome Pets.com Customers! PETsMART.com has purchased the www.pets.com URL.” The welcome coupon’s $25 minimum excluded dog food, cat food and cat litter.
“Pets.com is a division of WebMagic™… headed by Greg McLemore.”

note: Screenshots of Internet Archive captures, saved as images; click one to open the original capture. Other captures worth opening: the [May 1999 WebMagic-era home page](https://web.archive.org/web/19990508060549/http://www2.pets.com:80/), the [Nov 1999 holiday home page](https://web.archive.org/web/19991128201851/http://www.pets.com:80/cgi-bin/puppy/home/home.jsp?BV_UseBVCookie=YES&animal=Home) and the [Feb 2001 PETsMART.com redirect](https://web.archive.org/web/20010202130700/http://pets.com:80/). Many 1999 images were never archived.

captures.label: Anniversary sale
captures.title: Anniversary sale
captures.text: Eighteen days after the IPO: “Celebrate our Anniversary with 10% off Everything.” The sock puppet appears in the right column.

captures.label: Sock puppet gear
captures.title: Sock puppet gear
captures.text: The mascot had its own store category, “sock puppet gear”, alongside Dogs, Cats, Fish, Birds, Reptiles and Small Pets. Slate reported $20 puppets shipping in June 2000.

captures.label: The farewell letter
captures.title: The farewell letter
captures.text: The day after the shutdown, the homepage was replaced by a letter: “We have closed our virtual doors effective November 9, 2000.”
